content.jointProblem: Which combinations of moisture conditioning, machine condition, print settings and specimen geometry explain layer-boundary fatigue failures in OrtoPrint's PA12 components, and can affordable process changes reproducibly move fatigue life toward the required 500,000 cycles? The first experiment would test whether Erić's steel-focused fatigue and fracture-analysis approach transfers to PA12 by reproducing the baseline under a verified loading protocol and comparing matched, replicated specimens with controlled conditioning and documented machine and build histories.

rationale.text: Erić brings experimental fatigue-testing experience relevant to investigating cyclic failure, although the documented specimens were welded steel rather than printed PA12.

sources.quote: A total of 32 specimens were cycled at total strain amplitudes of 0.25%, 0.50%, 0.75%, and 1.00% using a servo-hydraulic machine

rationale.text: His work includes fracture-surface examination to distinguish failure modes, supporting investigation beyond visual inspection of finished parts.

sources.quote: Specimens failed either at the weld toe or in the weld metal, and failure locations were identified post-fracture by SEM.

rationale.text: He has experience linking industrial loading records to fatigue assessments, relevant to structuring the analysis of production and test histories.

sources.quote: Rainflow-counted stress spectra and simultaneous temperature records were used to construct a combined loading environment for assessment.

rationale.text: His published work combines local finite-element stress analysis with experimental fatigue validation, providing a basis for investigating geometry-related stress concentrations without assuming the existing models apply to PA12.

sources.quote: Finite-element-based stress analysis provides local stress amplitudes at the hinge throat for each counted cycle.
Experimental fatigue tests were conducted on twelve specimens; predicted lives agreed with measured lives within a factor of 2.1 in all cases

constraints.text: Validation must address the specified 500,000-cycle requirement at the relevant load and explicitly examine layer-boundary initiation; improved appearance or infill alone is not an acceptance criterion.

sources.quote: The test protocol calls for 500,000 cycles at the relevant load.
the fractures almost always initiate at layer boundaries rather than in the bulk material.

constraints.text: The intervention must remain compatible with the existing four-machine PA12 FDM process and a modest budget, without relying on replacement printers.

sources.quote: We print load-bearing components in PA12 nylon on four FDM machines
Budget is modest — we are not buying new machines — but we are open to process changes.

constraints.text: Process-data analysis requires access to the existing job logs and fatigue results, with specimen-to-job linkage established before attributing failures to process variables.

sources.quote: We keep print logs for every job — temperature, speed, layer height, humidity in the print room
We need someone to look at our process data and our test results and tell us what is actually driving the failures

constraints.text: Any production changes must be handled within the company's existing medical-device quality system; applicable revalidation obligations must be established before implementation.
Experimental workload must fit the company's limited development staffing and avoid assuming a dedicated full-time industrial research team.

sources.quote: We have two senior orthotists who contribute about 20% of their working time to product development and process improvement
supported by one mechanical technician who manages the print floor and test rig.

constraints.text: Any extended university test campaign requires advance equipment scheduling.

sources.quote: Erić's climate chamber and servo-hydraulic machine are shared with two other research groups; scheduling access for extended test campaigns requires advance coordination.

risks: The strongest evidence concerns welded steels, not PA12 inter-layer bonding, moisture sensitivity or polymer fatigue. The initial replicated PA12 experiment must test the transfer before adopting fracture models or life-prediction assumptions; polymer-processing support may be necessary.

Existing parameter changes produced inconsistent outcomes. Uncontrolled filament condition, machine differences, geometry or test-rig effects could confound historical correlations and prevent causal diagnosis.
Reaching 500,000 cycles is unvalidated and may not be achievable through affordable process changes alone.
Researcher availability is unknown. Although joint-project participation is open, the stated interests emphasize steel structures, so commitment to this polymer-medtech scope remains unconfirmed.
The numerical budget, deadline, test throughput and applicable device revalidation requirements are unknown; these could prevent sufficient replication or delay production implementation.
questions: Will Erić undertake a PA12-focused joint project, what time can he commit, and is a polymer additive-manufacturing collaborator needed?
What are the exact load waveform, amplitude, load ratio, frequency, fixture geometry, environment, failure definition and acceptance sampling requirements? When was the servo rig last calibrated?
Can each fatigue result and retained fracture specimen be linked to its CAD/build file, orientation, machine, filament lot, conditioning history and complete print log?
What PA12 grade is used, what drying procedure does its supplier specify, and are actual filament moisture, cabinet conditions and exposure between drying and printing measured?
Can the first campaign reproduce the baseline and compare controlled conditioning across matched specimens and machines, with enough replication to distinguish process effects from scatter?
What budget, deadline, specimen allowance and rig time are available, and which university characterization facilities can be scheduled within those limits?
Who approves process changes under the quality system, and what device-specific verification, revalidation and regulatory documentation will be required before release?
